facts.claim: Exposure to household air pollution is linked to a 19% increased risk of postnatal stunting.
facts.quote: A 19% increased risk of postnatal stunting (95% CI: 1. 10, 1. 29) was also associated with postnatal exposure to household air pollution.

facts.claim: Exposure to CO is not a consistently valid surrogate measure of exposure to PM2.5.
facts.quote: Our results suggest that exposure to CO is not a consistently valid surrogate measure of exposure to PM2. 5.

facts.claim: Household cooking with solid fuels accounted for 12% of APM2.5 globally in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, household cooking with solid fuels accounted for 12% of APM2.5 globally, varying from 0% of APM2.5 in five higher-income regions to 37% (2.8 μg/m3 of 6.9 μg/m3 total) in southern sub-Saharan Africa.

facts.claim: Household air pollution is linked to a substantial premature mortality burden globally of about 0.77(0.54-1) million excess deaths.
facts.quote: The median estimate indicates that the household contribution to ambient air pollution results in a substantial premature mortality burden globally of about 0. 77(0. 54-1) million excess deaths

rejected.claim: Household air pollution is linked to 35.7% (95% UI: 35. 6, 35. 9) of all PTB infants in 2019.
rejected.quote: 35. 7% (95% UI: 35. 6, 35. 9) of all PTB infants were attributable to total PM2. 5, equivalent to 5,870,103 (95% UI: 5,848,046 to 5,892,166) infants in 2019, respectively.

research.angle: Household air pollution from solid fuels is linked to significant global mortality, stunting, and infant health issues, though its contribution varies by region.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that household air pollution from solid fuels is a major driver of global mortality and developmental issues, but it does not specifically isolate 'rustic' wood smoke from fireplaces as a primary cause of cardiovascular risk.
research.caveat: Several studies note that the global burden of health impacts may have been underestimated due to limitations in exposure assessment and confounding factors.
